The AutoencoderKL family's convolution lines (bytes per output pixel, and a base in bytes) per operation and dtype, carried by vae.sd3 as the one member that runs all three dtypes; vae.sd, vae.flux and vae.flux2 borrow the lines of theirs. Fitted lines are working_memory/fit.py's: the upper envelope of the untiled single-sample in-fit points of every estimator resolving to this entry, plus 5%; the tiled points fit the tiled lines vae.sd, vae.flux and vae.flux2 carry themselves. Fitted on the RTX 4090 points (torch 2.13 and, for the older FLUX.2 rows, 2.7.1) of the SDXL VAE (fp16, fp32), the FLUX.1 VAE (bf16, fp32) and the FLUX.2 VAE (bf16, fp32). Where this entry prices a platform nothing is measured on (MPS, XPU, CPU, or another allocator on this backend), each slope is floored at the figure these estimators priced every dtype at before lines per dtype: 2200 bytes per pixel per element byte for a decode, 1100 for an encode. Refitted on its points by scripts/working_memory/build_shipped.py.

Fitted lines are working_memory/fit.py's: bf16 on the RX 9060 XT (gfx1200, torch 2.13+rocm10, Windows, expandable segments) tiled points of scripts/calibrate_vae_tiling_working_memory.py (2026-10-19: image sides 1024 to 12288 px with 512 and 1024 px tiles, and 2048 to 8192 px with 256 and 768 px tiles, the 256 px ones as lower bounds only), the tiled lines fitted on what they measured above the untiled demand these runs measured at their tile, and rated with the shipped untiled line there, the decode's together with its assembly line (`fit.two_phase_envelope`), each plus 5%. Stand-ins, no tiled point measures them: fp32 at, value by value, the larger of the SDXL VAE's tiled and assembly lines of the same operation and dtype on this platform and this family's own bf16 lines scaled by the element size (twice for fp32): the FLUX encoders emit 4 to 8 times the SDXL VAE's moment channels, and a FLUX decode's node and allocator show in its own lines. Refitted on its points by scripts/working_memory/build_shipped.py.

The CogView4 VAE's own lines: an AutoencoderKL, but not the family's stack (block widths 128/512/1024/1024, three layers per block, no mid-block attention), and a decode costs ~1.9x the family's. bf16 only: its loader forces it. Fitted lines are working_memory/fit.py's: the upper envelope of the untiled single-sample in-fit points of every estimator resolving to this entry, plus 5%. Windows only, where expandable segments are Invoke's ROCm default: measured on gfx1200 alone. Elsewhere they are a user override nothing is measured for, priced as MIOpen with the native allocator on that OS. Fitted on its RX 9060 XT (gfx1200, torch 2.13+rocm10) points.
